description:
Circuit Sages is a team of passionate innovators and problem-solvers exploring Earth's changing environmental systems through science, technology, and data analysis. Our goal is to identify environmental trends, visualize changes across regions, and uncover meaningful insights from Earth science data. We believe in innovation, collaboration, and using technology to build a smarter, more sustainable future.

Observe. Analyze. Decode. Discover.
summary:
Earth System Trend Detective is a website that lets anyone pick a city and a climate variable, see how it has changed since 1980, and check whether the change is statistically significant. It is built on NASA's MERRA-2 data.
Users can explore preset cities, draw their own 2° to 4° area to pull data directly from NASA Earthdata, or ask questions in plain language. A 3D globe lets them drop pins, and a short forecast sits alongside the long-term record.
It addresses the challenge by turning a large NASA dataset into something non-experts can use. Trends are tested with the Mann-Kendall test and Sen's slope, corrected for autocorrelation (Hamed and Rao, 1998). All statistics are computed in Python. The language model only writes the plan and the explanation, so it never produces the numbers.
This matters because people often see climate claims without any way to check them. The tool shows whether a change is real or just noise, using a method anyone can verify.
details: "Earth System Trend Detective lets anyone pick a city or draw an area and test whether a climate trend since 1980 is real. It uses NASA MERRA-2 data, Python (FastAPI), Next.js, CesiumJS and a Groq language model. Statistics are computed in Python and corrected for autocorrelation, and the AI only explains. It makes NASA data accessible, and we prioritised accuracy, speed and security."
dataRefs: NASA MERRA-2 (Modern-Era Retrospective Analysis for Research and Applications, Version 2)
